//: K-01/K-02's phoneme-to-id table: the EXACT vocabulary the pinned Kokoro ONNX export was built with, not a transcription of one. Extracted verbatim from tokenizer.json in onnx-community/Kokoro-82M-v1.0-ONNX -- the same Hugging Face repository and the same revision tools/mobile/fetch-models.mjs pins the weights from -- by reading model.vocab and re-emitting it in id order. source_sha256/source_bytes are the measured sha256 and length of that tokenizer.json; the same pair is pinned as the 'tokenizer' entry in fetch-models.mjs, so 'node tools/mobile/fetch-models.mjs --fetch' re-downloads the file this table came from and refuses it on a mismatch. Nothing here was typed by hand and nothing was inferred from a model card.
//use: Phonemes are mapped character by character: ids = [pad_id] + [table[c] for c in phonemes] + [pad_id]. A character absent from the table is a REFUSAL, never a skip -- kokoro-onnx's own loader filters unknown characters out silently, which turns a mis-phonemized word into a shorter word that still renders and still sounds like speech. The style vector is chosen by the UNPADDED id count, so dropping a character would also select the wrong row. 'max_input_ids' is the graph's own input_ids limit including both pads.
//vocab_id: tts.vocab, the string stamped on every phonemized item and checked by the player before it speaks (docs/bundled-voice-plan.md §5 item 8), is 'sha256:' plus the first 16 hex characters of the sha256 of this file's 'table' object serialised as compact JSON with sorted keys. tools/narration/phonemize.py's vocab_sha() computes it; tools/mobile/kokoro-vocab.test.mjs recomputes it in Node from the same bytes, so the two languages cannot drift.
